description: v5.5. Each room's temperature comes from ONE resolved template sensor (sensor.climate_temp_<room>) that owns source priority, per-sensor bias and usability gating. An implausible calibration offset is REPLACED BY THE MEASURED DEFAULT, never applied and never used to discard the source - a room must not lose its safety floor because a config number is wrong. The HOUSE decides heat vs cool from the outdoor temperature with exit-only hysteresis. Each ROOM has a day target and a night target plus an optional air-filter mode. SAFETY (frost / away floor / away ceiling) runs even when the comfort master is off, gated as a whole by input_boolean.climate_safety_always. Changes made outside this automation are detected from a per-room command timestamp versus the unit's own last_changed, and a unit that keeps changing itself is escalated as possibly faulty. Commanded setpoints are rounded to whole degrees and clamped to the unit's own min_temp/max_temp. Wind-free presets are applied to COOLING ONLY.

actions.note: The room list is an explicit ALLOW-LIST OF ACTUATED ENTITIES: the only entity this automation ever passes to a climate.* service is r.climate. The gas boiler and its Tado valves are NEVER commanded here. r.resolved and r.trv_watch are READ-ONLY. r.bad is the per-room 'sensor unusable since' stamp (R10-6); r.ext is the per-room 'last external change' stamp (R11 F11-4). Both are written by this loop only.

variables.house: {% set prev = states('input_select.climate_house_mode') %}{% if outdoor <= -900 %}shoulder{% elif heat_below_out >= cool_above_out %}shoulder{% elif prev == 'heat' %}{% if outdoor > heat_below_out + hyst %}{% if outdoor >= cool_above_out %}cool{% else %}shoulder{% endif %}{% else %}heat{% endif %}{% elif prev == 'cool' %}{% if outdoor < cool_above_out - hyst %}{% if outdoor <= heat_below_out %}heat{% else %}shoulder{% endif %}{% else %}cool{% endif %}{% else %}{% if outdoor <= heat_below_out %}heat{% elif outdoor >= cool_above_out %}cool{% else %}shoulder{% endif %}{% endif %}

actions.note: HOUSE MODE is a property of the weather, and it is STICKY with EXIT-ONLY HYSTERESIS. Round 10 (R10-4, R10-5) asked whether the memory can PIN the house in a season it should have left. It cannot, and the branch ORDER is what guarantees it: 'outdoor <= -900' (dead sensor) and 'heat_below >= cool_above' (inverted band) are both tested BEFORE prev is consulted, so each falls to shoulder unconditionally and the write-back below then CLEARS the remembered season. R10-3 is guarded in config health rather than fixed: hysteresis erodes the shoulder only as it approaches (cool_above - heat_below); with the live band 17->28 that is 11 C against a hysteresis of 1. The safety band reads neither helper and keeps running regardless.
Written back ONLY when it changes. It is the state memory the exit-only hysteresis needs.

if.value_template: {% set ns = namespace(bad=false) %}{% for r in rooms %}{% if r.trv_watch != '' %}{% set sp = state_attr(r.trv_watch,'temperature') | float(0) %}{% set at = (states(r.night_t) if night else states(r.day_t)) | float(20) %}{% if sp > at %}{% set ns.bad = true %}{% endif %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% set settle_bad = (states('input_number.climate_command_settle') | float(240)) < 60 %}{% set hyst_bad = (states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') | float(1)) < 0.5 %}{% set floor_bad = (states('input_number.climate_away_min') | float(18)) < 15 %}{% set frost_bad = (states('input_number.climate_frost_override') | float(7)) < 5 %}{% set trv_bad = (states('input_number.climate_trv_sensor_offset') | float(0) | abs) > 3 %}{% set ac_bad = (states('input_number.climate_ac_sensor_offset') | float(-2)) < -3.5 %}{% set hm = states('input_select.climate_house_mode') %}{% set house_bad = hm not in ['shoulder','heat','cool','unknown','unavailable'] %}{% set hyst_wide = (states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') | float(1)) >= (cool_above_out - heat_below_out) / 2 %}{{ heat_below_out >= cool_above_out or uptime > 34560000 or ns.bad or settle_bad or hyst_bad or floor_bad or frost_bad or trv_bad or ac_bad or house_bad or hyst_wide }}

data.title: Climate: configuration problem
data.message:
{% if heat_below_out >= cool_above_out %}**The house-mode band is inverted.** 'Heat below' ({{ heat_below_out }}) is not below 'Cool above' ({{ cool_above_out }}), so the house cannot resolve a season and ALL COMFORT HEATING AND COOLING IS STOOD DOWN. Only the safety band is still acting{% if not safety_on %} - and 'Safety limits always' is OFF, so NOTHING is protecting these rooms at all{% endif %}.

{% endif %}{% if uptime > 34560000 %}**The restart stamp is stale.** The guard that stops a post-restart fault being mistaken for a change made outside the automation is inert. Check automation.climate_stamp_ha_start.

{% endif %}{% set hm = states('input_select.climate_house_mode') %}{% if hm not in ['shoulder','heat','cool','unknown','unavailable'] %}**The house-mode memory helper holds an unexpected value** ('{{ hm }}'). The season boundary has fallen back to a bare threshold comparison, so the house can flap between heat and shoulder on a wandering outdoor reading. Recreate input_select.climate_house_mode with options shoulder, heat, cool.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') | float(1)) >= (cool_above_out - heat_below_out) / 2 %}**Hysteresis ({{ states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') }} C) is at least half the shoulder band** ({{ cool_above_out - heat_below_out }} C wide). At this width the exit threshold of one season reaches the entry threshold of the other and the neutral shoulder shrinks or disappears. Widen the band or narrow the hysteresis.

{% endif %}{% for r in rooms %}{% if r.trv_watch != '' %}{% set sp = state_attr(r.trv_watch,'temperature') | float(0) %}{% set at = (states(r.night_t) if night else states(r.day_t)) | float(20) %}{% if sp > at %}**{{ r.name }}: the radiator valve is set above the room's current target** (TRV {{ sp }} C vs {{ 'night' if night else 'day' }} target {{ at }} C). The boiler and the AC will alternate. Set the TRV at or below {{ at }} C.

{% endif %}{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_command_settle') | float(240)) < 60 %}**Command settle is {{ states('input_number.climate_command_settle') }} s** - below 60 s our own in-flight commands read as unit faults.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') | float(1)) < 0.5 %}**Hysteresis is {{ states('input_number.climate_hysteresis') }} C** - below 0.5 C rooms will flap at their target.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_away_min') | float(18)) < 15 %}**The away floor is {{ states('input_number.climate_away_min') }} C** - below anything safe for the cats or the pipes. It should be about 18.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_frost_override') | float(7)) < 5 %}**The frost override is {{ states('input_number.climate_frost_override') }} C** - too low to protect plumbing.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_trv_sensor_offset') | float(0) | abs) > 3 %}**The TRV sensor offset is {{ states('input_number.climate_trv_sensor_offset') }} C.** That is far larger than any plausible radiator-valve bias, so it is being IGNORED and the three bedrooms read their valves with no correction at all. A freshly created input_number comes up at its MINIMUM, which for this helper is -5: if that is what you are seeing, it was never set. It should be 0 until measured against a running radiator.

{% endif %}{% if (states('input_number.climate_ac_sensor_offset') | float(-2)) < -3.5 %}**The AC sensor offset is {{ states('input_number.climate_ac_sensor_offset') }} C** - larger than the measured return-air bias of about -2, so it is being IGNORED and every AC probe is corrected by the measured default instead. Readings are still trustworthy and the safety band is still protecting every room, but this number should be set back to about -2.

{% endif %}

actions.note: Silent failure modes, all of which pass a float() guard because the value is REAL but wrong. ROUND 11 (F11-5) gated the house-mode check so it does NOT fire on 'unknown'/'unavailable', which an input_select transiently holds during a reload or restart - otherwise this becomes a new cry-wolf on every boot, the exact R8-1 shape. The two offset messages were rewritten again: since v5.5 an implausible offset is REPLACED BY THE MEASURED DEFAULT rather than refused, so the operator needs to know the reading is still good and only the knob is wrong. This whole check writes ONE persistent notification with a FIXED id, so it replaces rather than stacks and never pushes to a phone - that is the throttle, and it is why R7-5 fatigue does not apply here.

sequence.note: ONE RESOLVED TEMPERATURE PER ROOM, SHARED BY EVERYTHING. If the sensor is unavailable or unknown it yields -999, the 'skip' sentinel: issue nothing, leave the room alone. ROUND 11 (F11-1) is why an implausible offset must NEVER produce that state: 'skip' is tested above every safety branch, so a room with no reading loses its frost and cat floors too.

variables.manual_active: {{ manual_ts is not none and now().timestamp() < (manual_ts | float(0)) }}
variables.since_cmd: {{ (now().timestamp() - (cmd_ts | float(0))) if cmd_ts is not none else 999999 }}

sequence.note: bad_ts/bad_armed/ext_ts are READ HERE, before any write later in this iteration, so the decision below uses the values as they stood at the START of the tick.

variables.unit_moved: {% set lc = (now() - states[r.climate].last_changed).total_seconds() %}{{ lc < since_cmd - settle and lc < human_window and lc < (uptime - 60) }}

sequence.note: THE IN-FLIGHT SIGNAL. THE FIRST TERM IS 'lc < since_cmd - settle', NOT 'lc < since_cmd'. A unit that OBEYS changes state about 1.5 s after we command it, so without the subtraction the term was true for ever after any successful command - a live bug on 2026-09-20 that stamped a hold and told the operator they had changed a unit they had not touched. KNOWN GAPS, both accepted: a person pressing a button INSIDE the settle window is not detected (operator's call, too rare to guard); and a unit that changes ITSELF inside the settle window is read as our own command, so the breaker counts it as a unit fault rather than an external move (R11 F11-8 - bounded and visible, but mislabelled). Both are the price of settle doing three jobs at once (R10-2, open).

variables.mode: {% if temp <= -900 %}skip{% elif safety_on and temp < frost %}heat{% elif safety_on and temp < away_min %}heat{% elif safety_on and temp > away_max %}cool{% elif manual_active %}manual{% elif not comfort %}off{% elif away or not enabled %}off{% elif house == 'heat' %}{% if temp < target or (now_mode == 'heat' and temp < target + hyst) or filter_on %}heat{% else %}off{% endif %}{% elif house == 'cool' %}{% if temp > target or (now_mode == 'cool' and temp > target - hyst) or filter_on %}cool{% else %}off{% endif %}{% else %}{% if filter_on %}fan_only{% else %}off{% endif %}{% endif %}
variables.want_target: {% if safety_on and temp > -900 and temp < frost %}{{ frost }}{% elif safety_on and temp > -900 and temp < away_min %}{{ away_min }}{% elif safety_on and temp > -900 and temp > away_max %}{{ away_max }}{% else %}{{ target }}{% endif %}

sequence.note: Precedence: skip > frost > away floor > away ceiling > manual hold > comfort. The three safety branches are gated on safety_on, so input_boolean.climate_safety_always is a genuine master hatch.

variables.set_target: {{ [[ (want_target | float(21)) | round(0) | int, umin | int ] | max, umax | int ] | min }}
variables.is_safety: {{ safety_on and temp > -900 and (temp < away_min or temp > away_max) }}

sequence.note: SETPOINT CLAMPING. The units report min_temp 16 / max_temp 30 / target_temp_step 1. Every commanded setpoint is rounded to a whole degree and clamped into the unit's own advertised range. The frost TRIGGER stays at 7 C; only the commanded setpoint is lifted to the unit's floor.

variables.target_ok: {{ (not needs_temp) or ((now_target | float(-1)) | round(0) | int) == set_target }}

variables.external_moved: {{ active and reachable and not mode_ok and not in_flight and unit_moved }}
variables.safety_throttled: {{ is_safety and manual_active and not throttle_ok }}
variables.no_temp: {{ safety_on and temp <= -900 and bad_armed and (now().timestamp() - bad_ts) > boot_grace and uptime > boot_grace }}

sequence.note: external_moved was called human_moved until round 10. It is not: the predicate can only see that the unit changed state for a reason that was not our command; it cannot tell a person at the wall from the Samsung app, a cloud push, a unit-side timer or a power restore, and there is no presence signal in this flat that could. ROUND 11 (F11-3) restored the BOOT GRACE alongside the per-room clock: no_temp now needs BOTH 'this room has been unusable for boot_grace' AND 'HA has been up for boot_grace'. They answer different questions - 'has this room been genuinely unreadable for ten minutes?' and 'is this just boot noise?' - and v5.4 kept only the first, which quietly re-armed the R8-1 cry-wolf for any cloud restore slower than 600 s. The uptime term is safe in both failure directions here BECAUSE it is an AND with the per-room clock: a stale ha_started makes uptime enormous, which simply stops suppressing and lets the per-room clock govern; a spurious mid-run write delays a genuine blackout alert by at most 600 s. That is the coupling round 9 rejected when uptime was the ONLY gate, and it is acceptable now that it is the secondary one. ext_recurring (F11-4) says this unit already changed itself within the last ext_window.

variables.may_act: {{ active and reachable and not mode_ok and not external_moved and not in_flight and not safety_throttled and (fail_count < breaker or is_safety or throttle_ok) }}
variables.will_set_temp: {{ active and mode_ok and needs_temp and not target_ok and not in_flight and not tripped and not safety_throttled }}
variables.will_set_preset: {{ active and mode_ok and mode == 'cool' and now_preset != preset and not in_flight and not tripped }}

variables.diverged: {{ active and reachable and not converged and not in_flight and not may_act and not external_moved and not will_set_temp }}

sequence.note: Divergence is only counted once our command has had its settle window AND we are not issuing a fresh command of our own this tick - neither a mode command (may_act) nor a SETPOINT command (will_set_temp).

data.title: {% if ext_recurring %}Climate: {{ r.name }} keeps changing itself{% else %}Climate: {{ r.name }} changed outside the automation{% endif %}
data.message: {% if ext_recurring %}**{{ r.name }} has now changed outside the automation twice within {{ (ext_window / 3600) | round(0) | int }} hours** (it reports '{{ now_mode }}'; we wanted '{{ mode }}'; the previous external change was at {{ states(r.ext) }}). If nobody is touching this unit, it is changing its own state - a schedule or eco timer set on the unit itself, a recurring power interruption, or a failing control board. Each event costs {{ manual_hold }} h of comfort control, so a unit doing this hourly is effectively never under automation. Worth checking the unit's own timer settings and its power supply.{% else %}{{ r.name }} reports '{{ now_mode }}'; the automation wanted '{{ mode }}'. Something outside this automation changed it - a remote, the Samsung app, a timer on the unit itself, or a power restore. Backing off for {{ manual_hold }} h so we do not fight it. Safety limits still apply, throttled to hourly while the hold is live.{% endif %}

data.title: {% if ext_recurring %}Climate: {{ r.name }} keeps changing itself{% else %}Climate: {{ r.name }} changed outside the automation{% endif %}
data.message: {% if ext_recurring %}Second external change within {{ (ext_window / 3600) | round(0) | int }} h - the unit may have its own timer or a power fault.{% else %}{{ r.name }} is in '{{ now_mode }}', we wanted '{{ mode }}'. Backing off {{ manual_hold }} h.{% endif %}

sequence.note: ROUND 11, F11-4. A unit that changes its own state on a recurring timer was invisible to BOTH detectors: every external move resets the breaker counter, and during the resulting hold the room is 'manual' so 'active' is false and the breaker cannot count at all - then the hold expires, the timer fires again, and a fresh hold is stamped. The room sits permanently outside comfort control while the operator receives an identical 'backing off' notice each time and is never told it is recurring. r.ext records when the last external change happened; a second inside ext_window (6 h) escalates the SAME notification id to a different message naming the likely causes. The hold behaviour is deliberately unchanged - backing off is still right whatever moved the unit - so this adds a diagnosis, not a new policy.

data.title: Climate: {{ r.name }} outside the safety band
data.message: {% if no_temp %}**{{ r.name }} has no usable temperature reading.** Its resolved sensor ({{ r.resolved }}) has been unusable since {{ states(r.bad) }}, so every source for this room is down at once. The safety band CANNOT be evaluated here - not because the room is fine, but because we cannot see it. Nothing will be commanded until a reading returns.{% else %}{{ r.name }} is at {{ temp | round(1) }} C, outside the {{ away_min }}-{{ away_max }} C safety band. {% if not reachable %}**The unit is {{ now_mode }} - we cannot command it at all.** Nothing this automation does will warm or cool this room until it comes back.{% elif converged %}The unit reports '{{ now_mode }}' at {{ now_target }} C, which is what we asked for, so it is nominally obeying - if the room is not recovering, the unit is losing to an open window, an undersized load or a mechanical fault.{% else %}The unit reports '{{ now_mode }}' at {{ now_target }} C; we want '{{ mode }}' at {{ set_target }} C.{% endif %}{% if manual_active %} A manual hold is live and the safety band is overriding it.{% endif %}{% endif %}

data.title: {% if no_temp %}Climate: {{ r.name }} sensor blackout{% else %}Climate: {{ r.name }} at {{ temp | round(1) }} C{% endif %}
data.message: {% if no_temp %}NO USABLE TEMPERATURE since {{ states(r.bad) }} - every sensor for this room is down, the safety band cannot be evaluated.{% else %}Outside the {{ away_min }}-{{ away_max }} C safety band. {% if not reachable %}Unit UNREACHABLE - cannot act.{% elif converged %}Unit says '{{ now_mode }}' and is obeying, room still out of band.{% else %}Unit says '{{ now_mode }}', we want '{{ mode }}'.{% endif %}{% endif %}

sequence.note: R6-4, R7-9, R8-1, rounds 9, 10 and 11. The alert follows THE CONDITION, never whether we managed to send a command.

data.title: Climate: {{ r.name }} isolated
data.message: {{ r.name }} did not reach '{{ mode }}' at {{ set_target }} C after {{ breaker }} attempts (it reports '{{ now_mode }}' at {{ now_target }} C). Comfort commands for this room are now throttled to hourly retries so one unresponsive unit cannot rate-limit the other four. Safety heating and cooling still run at full rate. It clears itself the moment the unit obeys.

data.title: Climate: {{ r.name }} isolated
data.message: {{ r.name }} AC not obeying '{{ mode }}' after {{ breaker }} tries. Comfort control throttled; safety limits still active.

sequence.note: The breaker is a THROTTLE, not a lockout: past the threshold the room still retries once every retry_throttle (3000 s).
The setpoint is only ever sent once the mode already matches. The is_state() re-read closes the same TOCTOU as the preset step.
WIND-FREE IS COOLING-ONLY. THE RE-READ IS A SAFETY INTERLOCK: climate.set_preset_mode on a unit that is OFF turns it ON, IN COOL (verified 2026-09-19 on the Office AC).

ROUND 10, R10-6. Written ONCE on the transition into unusable and cleared ONCE on the transition back, so flapping between unknown and unavailable does not touch it (both are the same side of the only question it asks); it is an input_datetime, so it survives a restart with its value intact and the grace expires on schedule rather than restarting.

The cleared sentinel is the year 2000 and 'armed' is tested as timestamp > 1e9, because a freshly created input_datetime reports TODAY 00:00 and is never none - a value that is plausible, wrong, and would read as 'bad since midnight'. The fail direction is the safe one: an unseeded helper makes the alert arm early, never late.
